robot.name: PAL Robotics TALOS
robot.status_notes: TALOS is a full-size torque-controlled biped from PAL Robotics, introduced around 2017 and sold to research labs. Official page says request a quote; ROBOTS guide lists status Ongoing and approximate cost €900,000. No public price or direct order page was found.
intended_use_cases: industrial tasks such as drilling or screwing (claimed)

height.notes: Official product page and ROBOTS guide both list 175 cm.

weight.notes: Official product page and ROBOTS guide both list 95 kg.

payload.notes: Per arm fully extended; product page says 6 Kg with each arm fully extended, ROBOTS guide says can lift 6 kilograms on each hand.

runtime.notes: Walking runtime about 1.5 hours; standby 3 hours per product page and ROBOTS guide.

battery.notes: Capacity not listed on product page; from ROBOTS guide.

degrees_of_freedom.notes: Breakdown from ROBOTS guide: Leg 6 DoF x2; Arm 7 DoF x2; Gripper 1 DoF x2; Waist 2 DoF; Neck 2 DoF. Product page does not list total DoF.

walking_speed.notes: Listed as Speed on ROBOTS guide; product page does not state walking speed.

hands.description: Customizable grippers, 1 DoF each; product page says head and gripper fully customizable.
hands.force_feedback: grippers do not have torque sensors (torque sensors in all joints except head, wrists and grippers)

items: Torque sensor feedback in all joints (except head, wrists and grippers per product page)
Force/torque sensors on wrists and ankles

compute.description: Two Intel Core i7 CPUs, Ubuntu LTS with Real Time OS, ROS, OROCOS, Gazebo simulation and URDF model, real-time ros_control loop at +1 kHz, MoveIt!

actuators.description: 32 high-torque brushless DC motors; torque sensors in all joints except head, wrists and grippers; EtherCAT communication network with 2 kHz control loops up to 5 kHz.

availability.notes: Official page says Request a quote. ROBOTS guide lists approximate cost €900,000, but no official price or online store.

manipulation_dexterity.summary: Product page claims 6 kg payload per arm fully extended and customisable grippers; ROBOTS guide says TALOS can lift 6 kg per hand and complete tasks such as drilling or screwing. No video transcript or independent demonstration was reviewed.
caveats: Official and directory claims only; no success rate, video evidence, or independent test available in reviewed sources.

autonomy_task_execution.summary: No evidence of autonomous task execution was found. Official product page mentions teleoperation as premium software, and ROBOTS guide lists both Fully Autonomous and Teleoperated features, but no autonomous demo or disclosure was provided. Video sources are titles only.
caveats: No video transcript or autonomy statement; teleoperation_status is not_disclosed for all demos.

mobility_whole_body_control.summary: Official page describes TALOS as a walking biped with torque control in all joints, EtherCAT control loops at 2–5 kHz, and provides whole-body control software. ROBOTS guide claims dynamic walking, including uneven ground and stairs, and 3 km/h speed. No video evidence reviewed.
caveats: Company/directory claims; no fall rate, disturbance recovery, or independent locomotion benchmark.

perception_scene_understanding.summary: Specs list RGB-D camera, IMU, force/torque sensors at wrists and ankles, and expansion modules for new sensors. No scene understanding demo or benchmark was found.
caveats: Sensor specifications only; no demonstrated perception capability.

human_interaction.summary: Product page lists HRI skills as premium software and customisable head/gripper; ROBOTS guide lists human-robot interaction skills. No interaction demo or evaluation found.
caveats: Claimed skill only; no conversational or interaction reliability metrics.

endurance_reliability.summary: Battery autonomy is 1.5 hours walking and 3 hours standby (1080 Wh lithium-ion per ROBOTS guide). No reliability data, failure rates, or maintenance logs were found.
caveats: Runtime is spec only; no long-duration operation or independent reliability evidence.

human_environment_fit.summary: TALOS is 175 cm tall and weighs 95 kg, with torque sensors in all joints for compliant interaction. Product page says it is Used globally in top labs driving robotics, AI, and human-centered tech. No safety certification found.
caveats: Size and weight may be large for home use; no safety certification or injury data.

deployment_commercial_proof.summary: ROBOTS guide lists status Ongoing and year 2017, with cost approximately €900,000. Video titles show arrivals at University of Waterloo and University of Edinburgh (SLMC), indicating research deployments. No commercial production metrics are available.
caveats: Deployment evidence is limited to video titles only; no units, hours, or task metrics.

accessibility_value.summary: No public price; official page requests a quote. ROBOTS guide lists approximate cost €900,000. Open-source URDF is available under Apache 2.0.
caveats: Approximate cost not official; no direct online purchase or subscription found.

evidence_items.title: TALOS product-page key specifications
evidence_items.claim: TALOS is a 175 cm, 95 kg walking biped capable of lifting 6 kg per arm fully extended, with battery autonomy 1.5 h walking / 3 h standby and customizable head and gripper.
evidence_items.notes: Official spec table and overview; values not independently measured.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Defines size, payload and runtime for comparison.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: A walking biped robot capable of lifting objects up to 6 kg with one arm fully extended.
evidence_items.source_location: TALOS product page, overview and technical specifications table
evidence_items.verification_notes: Company spec page. Payload per arm fully extended; runtime is walking/standby spec.

evidence_items.title: TALOS torque control claim
evidence_items.claim: TALOS has torque sensor feedback in all joints, enabling powerful sensing and multi-contact motions.
evidence_items.notes: Official claim; footnote says except head, wrists and grippers.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Torque control is central to whole-body control research claim.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: TALOS is fully torque-controllable thanks to the torque sensor feedback in all joints, which enables powerful sensing and multi-contact motions.
evidence_items.source_location: TALOS product page, torque control feature section

evidence_items.title: TALOS EtherCAT control frequency
evidence_items.claim: TALOS uses EtherCAT communication to run control loops at 2 kHz, and up to 5 kHz.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: High-frequency control supports dynamic whole-body motion.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: TALOS’ EtherCAT communication network allows to run control loops at 2 kHz, and up to 5 kHz, which enables TALOS to have highly reactive and dynamic motions.
evidence_items.source_location: TALOS product page, EtherCAT Network feature section
evidence_items.verification_notes: Company claim; no external bench test found.

evidence_items.title: TALOS ROS and premium software including teleoperation
evidence_items.claim: TALOS is ROS-based with open-source simulation model and premium software including whole-body control, navigation, HRI skills and teleoperation.
evidence_items.notes: Product page lists teleoperation as a premium software option.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Shows open software ecosystem; teleoperation availability is not autonomy.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Speed your research with extra software: from Whole-Body Control to navigation, HRI skills or teleoperation.
evidence_items.source_location: TALOS product page, premium software section
evidence_items.verification_notes: Official page; no specific teleoperation mode details.

evidence_items.title: TALOS degrees of freedom and compute
evidence_items.claim: TALOS has 32 DoF (Leg: 6 DoF x2; Arm: 7 DoF x2; Gripper: 1 DoF x2; Waist: 2 DoF; Neck: 2 DoF) and two Intel Core i7 CPUs.
evidence_items.notes: Directory listing; not from official PAL spec table.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Detailed DoF breakdown not available on official page.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Degrees of Freedom (DoF): 32 (Leg: 6 DoF x 2; Arm 7 DoF x 2; Gripper: 1 DoF x 2; Waist: 2 DoF; Neck: 2 DoF)
evidence_items.verification_notes: IEEE ROBOTS guide is reputable but secondary.

evidence_items.title: TALOS battery and power specs
evidence_items.claim: TALOS has a 1080-Wh lithium-ion battery with 1.5 hours walking and 3 hours standby operation.
evidence_items.notes: Battery capacity not on product page; directory spec.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Provides battery capacity missing from official page.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Power: 1080-Wh lithium-ion battery, 1.5 hours of operation walking, 3 hours of operation on standby
evidence_items.verification_notes: Secondary source; company runtime specs may vary in practice.

evidence_items.title: TALOS open-source URDF license
evidence_items.claim: TALOS URDF is available under Apache License 2.0 and PAL Robotics is interested in maintaining a MuJoCo model.
evidence_items.notes: GitHub issue submitted by PAL Robotics team member.
evidence_items.verification_notes: Company statement in issue; not a legal license file.

evidence_items.title: Cyberwave TALOS URDF derived from public repository
evidence_items.claim: Cyberwave hosts a TALOS URDF derived from a publicly available GitHub repository.
evidence_items.notes: Shows availability of a digital twin, but no capability data.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Confirms public model availability for simulation.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: This URDF is derived from the publicly available Github repository
evidence_items.verification_notes: Third-party platform; not verified against official PAL Robotics release.

evidence_items.title: Missing evidence for autonomy and capability verification
evidence_items.claim: No evidence of autonomous task execution, teleoperation status in demos, or independent verification of capabilities was found; video sources provided only titles.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Judges should reduce confidence on autonomy and task execution.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Gaps identified across all reviewed primary and secondary sources.
evidence_items.verification_notes: Absence of disclosure, not evidence of inability.

researcher_notes.short_verdict_for_arena: PAL Robotics TALOS is a long-standing torque-controlled research humanoid with strong open-source ROS support and claimed whole-body control, but the reviewed public evidence is mostly official specs and directory listings; no autonomous demo or independent verification was available.
strongest_positive_evidence: Official product page confirms 175 cm, 95 kg, 6 kg per-arm payload, 1.5 h walking runtime, torque sensors in all joints, EtherCAT 2–5 kHz.
ROBOTS guide lists 32 DoF, 1080 Wh battery, two Intel i7 CPUs, and approximate cost €900,000.
Public open-source URDF under Apache 2.0 and available via GitHub/Cyberwave.
Named research deployments indicated by video titles from University of Waterloo and University of Edinburgh.
weakest_or_missing_evidence: No autonomous task execution evidence or autonomy disclosure.
No video transcript or observable capability; all video evidence is title-only.
No public official price or direct purchase page.
conflicting_claims: Product page says torque sensors in all joints with footnote except head, wrists and grippers; ROBOTS guide says torque sensor feedback in every joint.
Product page lists no battery capacity; ROBOTS guide lists 1080 Wh.
Product page lists no walking speed; ROBOTS guide lists 3 km/h.
do_not_overclaim: Do not credit TALOS with autonomous operation; teleoperation status is not disclosed.
Do not treat ROBOTS guide's €900,000 as official price.
Do not describe video capabilities beyond titles.
Do not credit deployment metrics; only arrival videos with no task data.

arena_prompt_summary.one_paragraph_summary: PAL Robotics TALOS is a full-size biped humanoid (175 cm, 95 kg) introduced around 2017 and sold to research labs. Official evidence confirms 6 kg per-arm payload, 1.5 h walking runtime, torque sensors in most joints, and EtherCAT control loops up to 5 kHz; ROBOTS guide adds 32 DoF, 1080 Wh battery and approximate €900,000 cost. The robot is ROS-based with an open-source URDF under Apache 2.0. However, reviewed public evidence contains no autonomous task demonstration or capability video content beyond titles, and no commercial deployment metrics.
strongest_evidence: Official spec page: 175 cm, 95 kg, 6 kg per-arm payload, 1.5 h walking runtime, torque sensors in all joints except head/wrists/grippers.
ROBOTS guide: 32 DoF, 1080 Wh battery, two Intel i7 CPUs.
Open-source URDF under Apache 2.0 with public GitHub/Cyberwave models.
Named research arrivals: University of Waterloo and University of Edinburgh (video titles only).
weakest_evidence: No autonomous task execution demo or independent verification.
No video transcript; capabilities not observable.
No official price; approximate cost only.
No deployment metrics or reliability data.
known_do_not_credit: Walking on uneven terrain/stairs as verified.
